description: What the cloud is made of and how to use it well: its roots in virtualisation and distributed systems, the service and deployment models, architecture layers, security, service selection, economics and the major platforms, with real deployments on free tiers throughout. Taught to the depth of a leading cloud computing course and the foundational cloud certifications.
modelledOn: Buyya, Vecchiola and Selvi, Mastering Cloud Computing
NIST SP 800-145 The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing and NIST SP 500-292 Cloud Computing Reference Architecture
AWS Cloud Practitioner, Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) and Google Cloud Digital Leader objectives
Erl, Mahmood and Puttini, Cloud Computing: Concepts, Technology and Architecture
outcomes: Trace the technical roots of cloud computing and explain its essential characteristics.
Distinguish IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, FaaS and public, private, hybrid and community deployments and choose among them.
Describe cloud architecture layers and design applications for elasticity, resilience and multitenancy.
Apply the shared responsibility model and configure identity, network and data security in the cloud.
Select services using measurable attributes and compare providers on fit and cost.
Estimate and optimise cloud cost and operate services with monitoring, SLAs and service management practices.

units.title: Roots of cloud computing
topics: From mainframes and time-sharing to grids, utility computing, virtualisation and web services
Enabling technologies: virtualisation (hypervisors, containers), data centres, broadband, SOA and web APIs
The economics that made it work: scale, automation, pay-as-you-go
Cloud in Africa: regions in South Africa and Nigeria, latency to Ghana, local providers and data sovereignty

units.title: Characteristics, service models and deployment models
topics: Essential characteristics: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service
IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, FaaS/serverless, CaaS; the responsibility split at each level
Public, private, hybrid, community and multi-cloud deployments; edge and fog
Hands-on: launching a virtual machine, deploying an app to a PaaS, calling a serverless function

units.title: Architecture layers and methodologies
topics: Reference architecture: physical, virtualisation, orchestration, platform and application layers
Compute: VMs, containers, Kubernetes, serverless; storage: object, block, file; databases: managed relational, NoSQL, caches
Networking: VPCs, subnets, load balancers, CDNs, DNS
Design methodologies: well-architected pillars, twelve-factor apps, microservices, stateless design, infrastructure as code
Building a three-tier application on a cloud platform

units.title: Security in the cloud
topics: The shared responsibility model; threats specific to cloud (misconfiguration, credential leaks, insecure APIs)
Identity and access management: users, roles, policies, least privilege, MFA, federation
Network security: security groups, private subnets, bastions, WAF, DDoS protection
Data security: encryption at rest and in transit, key management, backups, data residency and the Data Protection Act
Compliance and assurance: ISO 27017/27018, SOC 2, audits; security monitoring and incident response

units.title: Service selection and SMI attributes
topics: The Service Measurement Index: accountability, agility, assurance, financials, performance, security and privacy, usability
Defining requirements and weighting attributes; multi-criteria decision making
Comparing providers and services for a case: a university LMS, a fintech API, a data analytics platform
Vendor lock-in and portability; open standards and open-source alternatives

units.title: Cloud economics: provisioning, cost optimisation, multitenancy, monitoring
topics: Pricing models: on-demand, reserved, spot, serverless; storage and egress costs; free tiers
Capacity planning and provisioning; autoscaling policies; right-sizing
Cost optimisation: tagging, budgets, alerts, FinOps practices; a worked estimate in dollars and cedis
Multitenancy: isolation models, noisy neighbours, SaaS tenancy design
Monitoring and observability: metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, alerting

units.title: Google, Azure and AWS platforms
topics: AWS core services: EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, VPC, IAM, CloudWatch
Microsoft Azure: Virtual Machines, Blob Storage, Azure SQL, Functions, Entra ID, Monitor
Google Cloud: Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Cloud Functions, IAM, Operations
Mapping equivalent services across providers; CLI and infrastructure as code (Terraform) for each
Deploying the same application to two providers and comparing

units.title: Service management
topics: Service level agreements, availability targets and credits; reading a provider's SLA
ITIL-aligned service management in the cloud: change, incident, problem, capacity
Backup, disaster recovery and multi-region design; business continuity
Capstone: a documented, secured, cost-estimated cloud deployment with monitoring and an SLA

schedule.title: Roots of cloud computing and its enabling technologies
schedule.exercise: Short essay: trace one idea (time-sharing, virtualisation or utility pricing) from its origin to a present-day cloud service, and say why it became practical only when it did.

tasks.title: Launch one virtual machine in the console, note its vCPU, memory and boot time, and stop it to see the metered usage change
Measure round-trip latency from an Accra office network to cloud regions in South Africa, Europe and the US, and tabulate which region suits an interactive app
Cost the same web workload on three owned servers versus pay-as-you-go instances over 12 months, then find the monthly utilisation at which owning becomes cheaper

schedule.title: Cloud characteristics and service models
schedule.exercise: Table exercise: for IaaS, PaaS, SaaS and serverless, list who manages each layer (hardware to data), and give one Ghanaian business example that suits each model.

tasks.title: Trigger an autoscaling rule by raising load on a one-VM service and observe rapid elasticity add instances, then check the measured-service usage report
Deploy the same small web app as a VM, as a PaaS app and as a serverless function, and compare setup steps, cost and what you must patch
Advise a fintech start-up in a branching case on IaaS versus PaaS versus serverless, justifying each decision with control, cost and staffing evidence to score on the rubric

schedule.title: Deployment models and hands-on provisioning
schedule.exercise: Design review: for a district hospital, a bank and a school, choose public, private, hybrid or community cloud and defend the choice in a paragraph each.

tasks.title: Launch a virtual machine, attach a firewall rule for port 80, and open the web page it serves from the console
Deploy a sample app to a PaaS, then call a serverless function that returns JSON, and record the latency of each call
Connect an on-premises office network to a cloud VPC over a VPN in a hybrid topology, and verify that private addresses reach each other without overlap

schedule.title: Reference architecture, compute, storage and networking
schedule.exercise: Draw a labelled five-layer cloud reference architecture and place ten named services (VM, object storage, CDN, load balancer and others) on the correct layer.

tasks.title: Create an object-storage bucket, upload three files, and compare it with attaching a block volume to a VM for the same data
Build a VPC with public and private subnets, a load balancer and two web VMs, and test that traffic reaches the private VMs only through the balancer
Debug a given cloud network whose private VMs cannot reach the internet or a database, by tracing routes, security groups and DNS records, and fix every fault

schedule.title: Design methodologies and the three-tier application
schedule.exercise: Assess a small existing app against the twelve-factor list and the well-architected pillars, and write a prioritised list of five changes with reasons.

tasks.title: Make a web VM stateless by moving its uploaded files to object storage, then replace the VM and confirm the files remain available
Build a three-tier application with a load-balanced web tier, an app tier and a managed database, and verify end-to-end requests from the console
Inject the failure of one availability zone into your three-tier deployment and redesign it so the service stays up with no data loss, then rerun the failure

schedule.title: Shared responsibility, identity and network security
schedule.exercise: Case write-up: a leaked access key caused a public bucket. Identify which controls from shared responsibility, IAM and network security would have prevented it.

tasks.title: Create an IAM user with a read-only policy for one bucket and confirm that delete and upload are refused
Place a database in a private subnet, expose a bastion host with a restricted source address, and verify access paths with security group rules
Audit a given account with an open storage bucket, a root key in use and a wide security group, then fix each issue using least privilege and re-audit

schedule.title: Data security, compliance and incident response
schedule.exercise: Map a Ghana Data Protection Act requirement to three technical controls, and write a one-page checklist for storing customer records in a cloud region.

tasks.title: Enable encryption at rest on a bucket and a volume, turn on versioning, and restore a deleted object from a previous version
Restrict a customer-data bucket to one region, enable key rotation and a backup rule, then show that cross-region copies are blocked by policy
Respond to a suspected cloud breach in a branching scenario by collecting log evidence, containing the account and notifying the regulator, scored against the rubric

schedule.title: Service selection and the Service Measurement Index
schedule.exercise: Build a weighted decision matrix with at least six SMI attributes to choose a provider for a campus learning platform, and justify each weight.

tasks.title: Score two cloud services on seven SMI attributes from 1 to 5 and compute their unweighted totals in a small table
Apply weights to a decision matrix for a fintech API, compute weighted scores for three providers, and test how the ranking changes when security weight doubles
Advise a company locked into one provider on an exit plan in a case scenario, weighing portability, open standards and migration cost against the rubric

schedule.title: Cloud economics: pricing, capacity and cost control
schedule.exercise: Estimate the monthly bill of a small web service in dollars and cedis, showing compute, storage, egress and a reserved-instance saving, and state your exchange-rate assumption.

tasks.title: Open the pricing calculator, price one VM, 100 GB of storage and 50 GB of egress for a month, and record each line item
Set an autoscaling policy for a traffic spike on a ticket-sales site, replay the load, and compare cost and response time with a fixed fleet
Cut the monthly bill of a given over-provisioned deployment by 30 percent using right-sizing, reserved capacity and budgets, while keeping response times under 300 ms

schedule.title: Multitenancy and monitoring
schedule.exercise: Design note: describe three tenancy models for a school-fees SaaS (shared schema, schema per tenant, database per tenant), and compare isolation, cost and onboarding effort.

tasks.title: Create a CloudWatch-style dashboard of CPU and request count for one VM and set an alarm that fires above 80 percent CPU
Run two tenants on one shared service, generate a noisy tenant load, and apply a per-tenant rate limit so the quiet tenant keeps its latency
Diagnose a slow application from metrics, logs and traces supplied by the console, identify the failing component, and define alerts that would have caught it earlier

schedule.title: AWS, Azure and Google Cloud platforms
schedule.exercise: Fill a comparison table of six core services (compute, object storage, relational database, serverless, identity, monitoring) across the three providers, and note one naming trap.

tasks.title: Complete a guided AWS-style walkthrough that starts an EC2 instance, creates an S3 bucket and reads a CloudWatch metric, and record each resource ID
Use Azure-style Blob Storage, a Function and Azure SQL to build a small API that stores uploads, and test it from the console
Build a Google-style stack with Compute Engine, Cloud Storage and Cloud SQL secured by IAM roles, and prove each role can do only its own task

schedule.title: Multi-provider mapping and portability
schedule.exercise: Write a short technical note comparing the same application deployed on two providers: setup time, price, features used, and what would stop you moving it.

tasks.title: Match twelve services from one provider to their equivalents on another using the mapping table, and check each match against its description
Run command-line commands to create a VM and a bucket, then write the same resources as a Terraform file and apply it in the terminal
Deploy one three-tier application to two provider consoles, record cost, latency and setup effort for each, and recommend one with evidence

schedule.title: Service management and capstone deployment
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: deliver the architecture diagram, security controls, monitoring plan, SLA target and a cost estimate in cedis for a documented cloud deployment.

tasks.title: Compute the yearly downtime allowed by 99.9, 99.95 and 99.99 percent availability targets and the service credit due for a given outage
Configure backups and a standby copy in a second region, fail over the primary on purpose, and measure recovery time and data loss
Build a capstone deployment with a load balancer, scaling policy, IAM roles, encrypted storage, monitoring alarms and a budget alert, then write its SLA target
